title: ModuleNotFoundError on Custom App After Fresh Install (Manual Ubuntu Setup)

posts.name: Paddy
posts.cooked:
I have a fresh manual installation of ERPNext on Ubuntu. I am trying to build a custom app (erpnext_voice) to integrate the Twilio Voice SDK.

I have created the app, a custom DocType (PR1 Voice Settings), and all the necessary files (.py, .js, hooks.py). However, when my frontend JavaScript tries to call a backend Python function, I consistently get the error:ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'erpnext_voice.erpnext_voice.doctype'

I have verified that all necessary __init__.py files exist in the correct directories. Here is the structure of my app:

apps/erpnext_voice
├── README.md
├── erpnext_voice
│ ├── init.py
│ ├── pycache
│ │ ├── init.cpython-312.pyc
│ │ └── hooks.cpython-312.pyc
│ ├── config
│ │ └── init.py
│ ├── doctype
│ │ ├── init.py
│ │ └── pr_voice_settings
│ │ ├── init.py
│ │ └── pr_voice_settings.py
│ ├── erpnext_voice
│ │ ├── init.py
│ │ └── pycache
│ │ └── init.cpython-312.pyc
│ ├── hooks.py
│ ├── modules.txt
│ ├── patches.txt
│ ├── public
│ │ ├── css
│ │ └── js
│ │ └── voice_client.js
│ ├── templates
│ │ ├── init.py
│ │ ├── includes
│ │ └── pages
│ │ └── init.py
│ └── www
├── license.txt
└── pyproject.toml

15 directories, 18 files

I have tried running bench build --force, bench migrate, bench clear-cache, and bench restart multiple times, but the Python environment does not seem to recognize the new module path.

Can anyone suggest a way to debug or fix the Python path for a custom app on a manual installation when the standard bench commands are not working?.

exact output is as follows
Failed to get method for command erpnext_voice.erpnext_voice.doctype.pr_voice_settings.pr_voice_settings.get_twilio_access_token with No module named ‘erpnext_voice.erpnext_voice.doctype’

Any Ideas appreciated , many thanks folks

posts.name: Abdeali Chharchhodawala
posts.cooked:
You are saying you created the PR1 Voice Settings but in doctype folder it is pr_voice_settings it should be pr1_voice_settings

and I am not sure but just, did you made doctype manually by creating files?

if yes, please delete it and make it from UI, frappe will automatically create files and save it to database

posts.name: Paddy
posts.cooked:
thank you for your response @Abdeali , actually you pointed out a typo to me in my description , I apologise , i will change that -

Actually in the end what was happening was purely down to python caching and stale files lying around causing misdirections

I was able to fix the issue by running the following commands to clear away these “ghost” files

find . -name “*.pyc” -delete

find . -name “pycache” -type d -exec rm -r {} +
